Shpock Scam UK: Spot a Fake Deal Safely

For collection deals, only hand over money when you're happy the item is as described and you're taking it home.

By Alex Bacsa · Published 2026-05-21 · Updated 2026-07-30 · 7 min read

Quick answer: Treat an upfront collection deposit, a supposed “Shpock courier”, or an unexpected payment link as a scam warning. Shpock says it does not provide its own courier, although buyers and sellers may arrange tracked shipping themselves. Inspect collection items before paying, keep messages in Shpock, and verify payment in your own account before posting an item.
Key rule: verify through an official route you opened yourself, not the link, number, app, or payment details supplied by the suspicious message.

Being targeted right now? Do this

  1. Stop. Don’t pay, transfer money, or share passwords, PINs, or one-time codes.
  2. Contact your bank on the number on the back of your card if your money or details may be at risk.
  3. Use the right recovery route. Follow the payment, account and identity checklist; reporting differs in Scotland.

What a Shpock scam looks like

A Shpock scam may involve an upfront deposit before a collection, a supposed “Shpock courier”, or an unexpected courier or payment link designed to collect card details. Shpock says it does not provide its own courier service. That is different from self-organised shipping: buyers and sellers may agree postage themselves, ideally using tracked or insured delivery. A genuine seller discussing ordinary postage in the offer process or private sales chat is not, by itself, evidence of fraud.

An example of the pressure style: I've had a lot of interest, pay a £20 deposit now to hold it and I'll see you at the weekend.

Why it's convincing

Many ordinary Shpock deals involve collection or postage arranged by users. Some still-accessible Shpock Help Centre pages describe the former Buy Now, Wallet and Secure Delivery flow, while current app listings describe local collection or self-organised shipping. That mixed-era documentation can make a fake “Shpock courier” or payment message sound plausible, especially to someone who remembers the former service.

Shpock's discontinuation notice names the Buy Now feature and Shpock Wallet only, and it gives no year. That Secure Delivery is also no longer the live flow is an inference from that notice and the current app listings, not a separate formal statement Shpock publishes on the pages cited below.

Signs a Shpock deal is a scam

  • You are asked for a deposit before inspecting a collection item.
  • Someone claims that a “Shpock courier” will collect or deliver the item.
  • You receive an unexpected courier or payment link asking for card or account details.
  • You are pushed to move the conversation out of Shpock.
  • A seller pressures you to pay immediately, or a buyer pressures you to post based on an email, screenshot or pending-payment message rather than money you can verify in your own account.

How the scam works step by step

First, a seller or buyer asks for a deposit or payment before the item is collected or verified, or sends a fake courier or payment link in chat. Second, you pay by bank transfer or a payment method whose recovery route is limited or conditional, or you enter card details on the linked page. Third, the item never existed, is not as described, or the courier arrangement was never real.

Recovery may be difficult, but it is not automatically impossible. Contact the relevant bank or payment provider immediately and ask which fraud, recall, reimbursement or dispute route applies. Our scam recovery checklist sets out the steps in order.

How to buy and sell safely on Shpock

For collection, meet safely, inspect the item and pay only when you are satisfied and taking it home.

  • Keep the conversation in Shpock and preserve the listing, offer and chat.
  • Agree the payment method, shipping method and postage cost before accepting the offer.
  • For delivery, use tracked or insured shipping and keep the receipt and tracking evidence.
  • Never use an unexpected courier or payment link sent in chat. Open your bank or payment provider independently.
  • For delivery, if you independently choose PayPal, use a Goods and Services payment and check the item and transaction against PayPal's current Buyer Protection terms. Friends and Family payments are excluded. PayPal says an Item Not Received claim is not eligible when a physical item is collected in person or collected on your behalf, except for an eligible in-person Goods and Services QR-code transaction. This is PayPal protection, not Shpock protection.
  • If you are selling: Confirm payment in the bank or provider account you open independently. If it is pending or anything looks unusual, contact the provider before releasing the item. An email, screenshot or buyer-supplied status page is not proof.

If you've already paid a deposit or clicked a link

Contact the relevant bank or payment provider immediately and ask which fraud, recall, reimbursement or dispute route applies. If you used PayPal, check the exact transaction against the current Buyer Protection terms; Friends and Family payments are excluded, and an Item Not Received claim normally excludes a physical item collected in person or on your behalf. The stated exception is an eligible in-person Goods and Services QR-code transaction, so check which case applies. If it is eligible, open the dispute in PayPal's Resolution Centre without delay.

Opening a link alone does not automatically mean a password must be changed. The next step depends on what happened: whether you entered credentials or card details, paid, downloaded or opened a file, installed an app or profile, granted remote access or another permission, or noticed unusual device behaviour. Follow the relevant NCSC recovery branch. The NCSC's phishing response and recovery guidance at ncsc.gov.uk sets out those branches.

  • If you entered card details, contact the card issuer.
  • If you entered a password, change it through the genuine service and change it anywhere it was reused.
  • Preserve the listing, profile, chat, link, payment record and tracking evidence.

How to report a Shpock scam (UK)

Shpock's live “Reporting another user” page says that, for a collection deal, open the chat, tap the three dots and choose “Report partner”. For a delivery deal, open the chat, tap “Help” and choose “Report user”. To report a prohibited or suspicious listing, scroll to the bottom of the item screen and choose “Report this listing”.

If money was lost, report it to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or on 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or to Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland.

Frequently asked questions

Should I pay a deposit to secure a collection item on Shpock?

Treat it as a red flag. Shpock's buying guidance is to hand over money for collection only when you're happy the item is as described and you're taking it home.

Does Shpock have its own courier service?

No. Shpock says it does not provide one. Buyers and sellers may agree self-organised tracked shipping, so delivery itself is not proof of fraud. A supposed “Shpock courier” or an unexpected courier or payment link asking for details is the warning. Report the other user in a collection deal from the chat's three-dot menu using “Report partner”, or the other user in a delivery deal through “Help” and “Report user”.

Does Shpock currently provide Buyer Protection?

Do not assume Buyer Protection is available for a new deal. Shpock's live materials conflict: its discontinuation notice says Buy Now and Wallet ended, current app listings describe collection or self-organised shipping, while older help and terms still describe former protection. Rely only on what the current app offers for that specific deal and read the applicable payment provider's current terms. If you independently use PayPal Goods and Services, any protection is PayPal's and depends on PayPal's eligibility rules and deadlines: Friends and Family payments are excluded, and PayPal says an Item Not Received claim is not eligible when a physical item is collected in person or on your behalf, except for an eligible in-person Goods and Services QR-code transaction.

I paid a deposit and the seller disappeared. Can I get my money back?

Contact your bank or payment provider immediately and ask which fraud, recall, reimbursement or dispute route applies — recovery may be difficult but is not automatically impossible. If you paid by PayPal Goods and Services, check the exact transaction against PayPal's current Buyer Protection terms before assuming a claim will succeed: Friends and Family payments are excluded, and an Item Not Received claim is not eligible for a physical item collected in person or on your behalf, except for an eligible in-person Goods and Services QR-code transaction. Keep the listing, chat and payment record, then work through the scam recovery checklist.

How do I report a scam on Shpock?

For a collection deal, open the chat, tap the three dots and choose “Report partner”. For a delivery deal, open “Help” and choose “Report user”. To report a listing, scroll to the bottom of the item screen and choose “Report this listing”. If you lost money, report it to Report Fraud at reportfraud.police.uk or 0300 123 2040 in England, Wales or Northern Ireland, or to Police Scotland on 101 in Scotland.

Fast checks

  • Pause before sending money or credentials
  • Verify with an official site, app, or number
  • Never share one-time passcodes
  • Be sceptical of bank transfer pressure
